# External numerical reference fixtures

These compact files preserve outputs generated by implementations outside
SpectralSelector. Normal tests consume only the stored values, so the external
package is not a test-time dependency.

`chemotools_0_4_3_vip_sr.json` was produced with chemotools 0.4.3
`VIPSelector` and `SRSelector`, using scikit-learn `PLSRegression` with three
components and scaling disabled. The analytic input construction is reproduced
in `tests/test_model_based.py`. Both X and y are explicitly centered because
the two implementations otherwise differ in where target-projection centering
is performed. The recorded threshold is 1.0; no fixture score lies exactly on
the boundary, avoiding a `>` versus `>=` policy difference.

`plsvarsel_0_10_0_covsel.json` was produced with the R package plsVarSel 0.10.0
`covSel` function. The fixture records zero-based selected indices and
cumulative explained X/Y fractions reconstructed from the external normalized
scores and loadings. The analytic multi-response inputs are reproduced in
`tests/test_covsel.py` and `tests/test_fcovsel.py`. Although exported as
`covSel`, this version of the external function constructs candidates from the
original X, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalizes its scores, and deflates Y without
repeatedly deflating X. Its selected order therefore also supplies an external
check of the local fCovSel sequence. The fixture does not assume that absolute-
and squared-covariance aggregation are universally equivalent for multiple
responses. Only numerical outputs and provenance are retained; the external
GPL-licensed implementation is not copied into SpectralSelector and R is not
required by the test suite.

`sklearn_1_9_0_pls_component_search.json` was produced by directly evaluating
scikit-learn 1.9.0 `PLSRegression` candidates with an explicit shuffled
four-fold split. It records every fold score and mean score for one analytic
matrix, independently of the CARS and BOSS search methods. The fixture checks
their shared component-search result; separate tests isolate the lower bound,
the configured/subset-width/sample-rank upper bounds, and the deterministic
preference for fewer components on a score tie. It does not validate either
method's complete stochastic trajectory or claim equivalence to author code.

When updating a fixture, retain the old file unless the upstream result was
demonstrably incorrect. Record the external package version, complete model
configuration, input construction, expected scores, selected indices, and a
numerical tolerance justified by floating-point reproducibility.
